name: BachPreludeInC
listen_for: Bach's C major prelude on the standard set's two-choir harpsichord in a large room, each figure ringing on under the next, leaning into the bars where the harmony arrives and slowing into a rolled last chord.

name: PassionChorale
listen_for: Bach's Passion Chorale for the standard set's trumpet, French horn and trombone and a flugelhorn of its own, in a hall, every phrase slowing into its fermata and taking a breath, the repeat an echo of the first time.

name: FurElise
listen_for: Für Elise on the standard set's tine electric piano, swaying between the speakers in a large room, pedalled bar by bar, broadening into each cadence, pressing on over the drumming bass and slowing down the chromatic scale.

name: HallOfTheMountainKing
listen_for: Grieg's trolls, orchestrated from the piano score for the standard set's orchestra in a concert hall: bassoons and pizzicato basses tiptoe through the theme, which climbs, gathers the orchestra and speeds up until the trolls shriek over the timpani.

name: BachInventionInF
listen_for: Bach's two-part invention in F as an old games console would play it, a pulse wave for the right hand and a triangle for the left, chasing each other across the speakers in a small room: a whole piece the NUCLEO-L476RG plays.

name: TheEntertainer
listen_for: Joplin's rag on the standard set's honky-tonk piano, an old upright whose unisons have drifted apart, in a large room, not fast and steady as he asked, its bass striding under the syncopated tune, the second time through the B strain an octave up, as marked.

name: SoldiersJoy
listen_for: A fiddle tune as an old-time string band plays it for a dance, three times through: the fiddle kicks off and leads, the banjo takes the tune the second time while the fiddle shuffles chords behind it, and the guitar's boom-chuck and the bass keep the beat.

name: Kappore
listen_for: A street dancer's song from Edo for the standard set's shakuhachi and koto, the koto following the tune an octave down: the first verse unhurried, the second pressing on with a bamboo flute above, taiko and the kane's chan-chiki, and the clappers quickening at the end.

name: MapleLeafRag
listen_for: Joplin's rag as a New Orleans band would swing it: cornet lead with the clarinet a third or sixth above and the trombone smearing in under them, the clarinet alone the second time, a stop-time strain, the trio's first time on piano, and the banjo, tuba and drums driving the last strains home.
